skill.name: swiftui-ui-patterns
skill.description: Best practices and examples for building SwiftUI views, navigation, sheets, forms, lists, grids, and app wiring.
skill.summary: SwiftUI reference patterns for composing accessible, maintainable app interfaces.
skill.author: Dimillian

security_audit.summary: The static findings are false positives caused by Markdown formatting, SwiftUI API names, UI best-practice wording, keyboard shortcuts, and a placeholder example URL. I found no evidence of prompt injection, malicious intent, data exfiltration, credential access, or unsafe command execution.

content.value_statement: SwiftUI teams need repeatable patterns for navigation, sheets, forms, lists, and app wiring. This skill provides focused guidance and examples for building maintainable Apple platform interfaces.
actual_capabilities: Guides TabView, NavigationStack, sheet, form, list, grid, and split-view composition.
Provides SwiftUI examples for app wiring, environment injection, and route handling.
Explains UI patterns for loading placeholders, search, focus, haptics, and media views.
Highlights pitfalls for layout performance, state ownership, navigation history, and accessibility.
Supports both new SwiftUI screens and refactors inside existing Apple platform apps.
limitations: It is a guidance library, not a package that compiles into an app.
Examples use generic types that must be adapted to each project.
It does not replace platform documentation or project-specific design review.
It does not provide production networking, persistence, or authentication implementations.

use_cases.title: Plan a New SwiftUI App Shell
use_cases.description: Use the app wiring, TabView, NavigationStack, and sheet patterns to define the first application structure.
use_cases.target_user: iOS engineer starting a new app

use_cases.title: Refactor Existing Screens
use_cases.description: Apply focused guidance for forms, lists, grids, overlays, and loading states while preserving local conventions.

use_cases.title: Standardize Team UI Practices
use_cases.description: Use the component references to document shared decisions for navigation, theming, menus, and accessibility.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Pattern
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for selecting the right SwiftUI reference.
prompt_templates.prompt: I am building a SwiftUI screen with a list, detail view, and sheet. Which references should I use, and why?

prompt_templates.title: Draft a Screen Structure
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request for planning a new feature screen.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design the structure for a SwiftUI settings screen with grouped forms, validation, and a dismiss action.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor Navigation
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for improving navigation and routing.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this SwiftUI navigation approach and align it with independent tab histories and route enums.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a UI Architecture
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for cross-component architecture review.
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit my SwiftUI app shell for state ownership, dependency injection, sheets, deep links, and loading behavior.

output_examples.input: A developer asks how to build a tabbed SwiftUI app with independent navigation history.
output: Recommend one NavigationStack per tab with a small router object for each path.
Use a shared destination mapping only when it avoids duplicate route switches.
Keep route data lightweight and avoid storing view instances in navigation paths.

output_examples.input: A team wants to improve a modal form that saves a remote server URL.
output: Use Form inside a NavigationStack when the view is presented alone.
Keep validation state local and disable the save action until the input is valid.
Use focused fields and keyboard settings that match the expected input type.

output_examples.input: A maintainer asks why a media grid feels slow while scrolling.
output: Prefer LazyVGrid for large collections and keep spacing predictable.
Use resized thumbnails in rows and avoid loading full-size images in repeated cells.
Move expensive overlays out of every cell when possible.

best_practices: Start with the component reference that matches the primary interaction model.
Keep SwiftUI state local unless shared services or routing require environment injection.
Validate examples against the existing project style before adding new abstractions.
anti_patterns: Do not add view models when local SwiftUI state is enough.
Do not mix multiple sheet patterns for the same presentation concern.
Do not copy generic examples without adapting names, routes, and dependencies.

faq.question: Does this skill generate complete SwiftUI apps?
faq.answer: No. It provides patterns and examples that help structure app views and components.

faq.question: Can I use it with an existing codebase?
faq.answer: Yes. Start by matching the current screen type to the closest reference, then follow local conventions.

faq.question: Does it support macOS interfaces?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes guidance for menu bars, settings, split views, and Apple platform UI patterns.

faq.question: Does it include networking guidance?
faq.answer: It includes lightweight client structure, but it does not implement production network security or authentication.

faq.question: Is this useful for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The references are written for coding agents that can read files and apply SwiftUI patterns.

faq.question: Should I follow every example exactly?
faq.answer: No. Treat examples as starting points and adapt them to your project types and design system.
